title: Virginia Car Tax Calculator (Personal Property Tax)
description: Estimate your Virginia personal property (car) tax. Enter your vehicle's assessed value, your locality's rate per $100, and PPTRA relief to see your gross tax, the state subsidy, and what you actually owe.
answerSnippet: Virginia car tax = assessed value ÷ 100 × your locality's rate. On a $20,000 vehicle in Fairfax County at $4.57 per $100 with 49% PPTRA relief on the first $20,000, the gross tax is $914 and you pay about $466.
intro:
Virginia is one of the states that charges an annual **personal property tax on vehicles** — often called the **'car tax.'** Each city and county sets its own **rate per $100** of a vehicle's **assessed value** (usually the **J.D. Power / NADA clean trade-in** value as of January 1). Rates typically run from about **$3.09 to $5.00 per $100**.

A big part of the bill can be offset by the **Personal Property Tax Relief Act (PPTRA)**. The Commonwealth subsidizes a percentage of the tax on the **first $20,000** of assessed value for **qualifying personal-use vehicles**. Each locality sets its own **relief percentage** each year (for example, **49% in Fairfax County for 2026**).

Enter your vehicle's **assessed value**, your **locality's rate**, and your **PPTRA relief percentage** to see the gross tax, the relief, and what you actually owe.
keyTakeaway: Car tax = **assessed value ÷ 100 × local rate**. PPTRA subsidizes a set percentage of the tax on the **first $20,000** for personal-use vehicles; value above $20,000 gets **no relief**. Rates and relief percentages are set **locally each year** — Arlington and Alexandria are $5.00/$100, Fairfax $4.57, Loudoun $3.09. Assessed value is normally the J.D. Power clean trade-in as of January 1.

explanation:
## How Virginia car tax is calculated

```
Gross tax   = assessed value ÷ 100 × local rate
Relief base = first $20,000 of assessed value (personal-use vehicles)
PPTRA relief = (relief base ÷ 100 × local rate) × relief %
Tax you owe  = gross tax − PPTRA relief
```

**Assessed value** is set by your locality, generally the **J.D. Power (NADA) clean trade-in** value as of **January 1** (Arlington uses a 'clean loan' value; Loudoun moved to **MSRP-based** assessment for 2026). Higher-value cars pay full rate on everything **above $20,000**, since relief only touches the first $20,000.

## 2026 rates for major Virginia localities

| Locality | Rate per $100 | PPTRA relief |
|---|---|---|
| Arlington County | $5.00 | varies |
| Alexandria City | $5.00 | varies |
| Fairfax County | $4.57 | 49% |
| Virginia Beach | $4.00 | varies |
| Prince William County | $3.70 | varies |
| Richmond City | $3.70 | varies |
| Loudoun County | $3.09 | 41% |

Rates and relief percentages are set **each year** by each locality — always confirm the current figures with your city or county.

## Why the same car costs different amounts

Two identical cars can owe **different** tax in different counties because both the **rate** and the **assessed value method** differ. A $4.57 rate in Fairfax and a $3.09 rate in Loudoun on the same value produce very different bills, and Loudoun's MSRP-based assessment can change the value itself.

## Disclaimer

Educational estimate. Your actual bill depends on your locality's official assessed value, current rate, relief percentage, any prorating for part-year ownership, and vehicle-type rules. Confirm with your city or county tax office.

faq.q: How is Virginia car tax calculated?
faq.a: It is your vehicle's **assessed value ÷ 100 × your locality's rate**. For example, a $20,000 car at $4.57 per $100 has a **$914** gross tax before any PPTRA relief.

The **Personal Property Tax Relief Act** has the Commonwealth subsidize a percentage of the tax on the **first $20,000** of assessed value for **qualifying personal-use vehicles**. Each locality sets its relief percentage yearly — for example, **49% in Fairfax County for 2026**.

faq.q: How is my vehicle's assessed value determined?
faq.a: Most localities use the **J.D. Power (NADA) clean trade-in** value as of **January 1**. Arlington uses a 'clean loan' value, and **Loudoun County switched to MSRP-based** assessment for 2026, so the same car can be valued differently by locality.

faq.q: Which Virginia county has the highest car tax rate?
faq.a: **Arlington County** and **Alexandria City** are among the highest at **$5.00 per $100**. **Loudoun County** is lower at **$3.09**. Fairfax is **$4.57**. Rates change annually, so verify locally.

faq.q: Do vehicles worth over $20,000 get relief?
faq.a: Only on the **first $20,000** of assessed value. The portion **above $20,000** is taxed at the full rate with **no** PPTRA relief, so expensive vehicles have a higher effective rate.

faq.q: Does business use change the tax?
faq.a: Yes. **PPTRA relief applies only to personal-use vehicles.** A vehicle used predominantly for **business** generally does not qualify for relief, so you would owe the full tax.

faq.q: When is Virginia car tax due?
faq.a: Due dates are set by each locality — commonly in **October**, sometimes split into two payments. Check your city or county tax calendar, since a late payment can add penalties and interest.

faq.q: Do I still owe car tax if I move mid-year?
faq.a: Localities generally **prorate** the tax for the portion of the year you owned or garaged the vehicle there. If you move between Virginia localities, you may owe a prorated amount to each. Confirm with both tax offices.
